name: Gotify
tagline: A self-hosted push notification server with a simple REST API and its own Android app.

local.note: Push only works while this computer is on, so an alert that arrives after sleep waits until the machine wakes, and a phone on cellular cannot reach localhost.

quote.text: We wanted a simple server for sending and receiving messages (in real time per WebSocket).

citations.claim: Upstream documents a Docker install that stores state in a mounted data directory and serves HTTP on port 80 inside the container.
The first admin user can be seeded with GOTIFY_DEFAULTUSER_NAME and GOTIFY_DEFAULTUSER_PASS environment variables.
Clients authenticate with application tokens when sending messages and client tokens when receiving them.
There is an official Android app; there is no first-party iOS app in the same repository family.
Caddy obtains and renews TLS certificates automatically for any public hostname named in the Caddyfile.

whatYouSignUpFor: There is no first-party iOS app. Android has the official Gotify client; iPhone users need a third-party client or another path such as ntfy.
You own the backups. The SQLite database under data/ and the .env file that holds the seeded admin password are the install. A restore without .env is a lockout.
You own delivery. If the box is down, nothing reaches the phone, and nobody else is watching the watcher.
Admin credentials are generated on the server into .env, never written into the compose file as standing defaults.
Message retention and plugins are yours to configure. Defaults will not match a cloud product's multi-year archive story.
